messages:
marta: Heads-up — running into surprising behavior with the Go SDK generator streaming API and context cancellation. Repro below and curious if this is a parity bug or my misuse.

marta: Repro (Go, go-redwood v0.9.1):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
gen := client.NewGenerator("gpt-foo", client.WithAPIKey(key))
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, &GenerateRequest{Prompt: "large prompt...", MaxTokens: 1024})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

// consume in separate goroutine
go func() {
  for {
    tok, err := stream.Next()
    if err != nil {
      log.Println("stream ended:", err)
      return
    }
    fmt.Print(tok.Text)
  }
}()

// cancel after a bit
time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
cancel()
// expecting stream.Next() to return context.Canceled or io.EOF, but goroutine hangs
```

marta: Observed: goroutine stuck on stream.Next() forever, underlying HTTP request still active, CPU idle. Only way to unblock is process exit. Tried calling stream.Close() — no Close on type (there's a Close() on old Reader API but not the new generator stream). Feels like missing Close/cancel propagation.

josh: Ugh. I hit something like this last week when trying to integrate streaming into our webhook worker. The HTTP client context should be tied to ctx; if stream.Next() blocks something's not propagating. Did you try changing gen.Stream(ctx) -> gen.Stream(context.WithTimeout(...)) as a temp workaround?

marta: Yep tried WithTimeout and it still hung until deadline. Also tried using httptrace to confirm the socket stays open.

kai: @marta thanks for the clear repro. Two quick Qs: can you paste the module version in go.mod (go-redwood v0.9.1?) and whether you used the streaming option with Delta vs. Token mode? Also, does the non-streaming Generate call respect ctx cancel for you?

marta: go.mod shows github.com/redwood-inference/go-redwood v0.9.1
marta: Non-streaming Generate(ctx, req) cancels as expected (returns context.Canceled). Only stream.Next() seems stuck.

sam: Sounds like an ergonomics gap: Stream returns an iterator but no Close() or Cancel() method. Patterns in other Go clients: expose Close() on stream and make Next() return io.EOF after Close. Also the generator's Stream should spawn a goroutine and select on ctx.Done() to stop underlying reads.

josh: Agree on ergonomics. For parity, our Python/TS SDKs have stream.close() / iterator.throw() semantics. Go should match: stream.Close() and stream.Err() or return context.Canceled.

kai: I'll try to repro on my machine. If it's a bug we'll patch the runtime to ensure the request is canceled when ctx.Done() fires and add a Close() on the stream type. @marta could you attach the tcpdump/trace you mentioned? devex-bot: please label this bug "go-sdk:stream-cancel-leak".

marta: Attaching short tcpdump in thread (snippet):
```
15:02:34.123 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > api.redwood: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 32768
15:02:34.329 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > api.redwood: Flags [P.], seq 512:1024, ack 1
// no FIN after cancel
```

devex-bot: label added: go-sdk:stream-cancel-leak

marta: Minimal repro gist: https://gist.github.com/marta/repro-go-stream-cancel (contains same code above + go.mod). Please try.

kai: I reproduced locally on Linux, appears to be that the generated stream reads from the response body in a blocking read without selecting on ctx.Done(). I'll open a PR to 1) ensure the http.Request uses ctx (it already does) and 2) add an explicit stream.Close() that closes the underlying response body and causes Next() to unblock.

josh: API ergonomics: make Close() a method and update docs/examples. Also consider adding a helper: gen.StreamWithContext(ctx, opts) returns (stream, cancel) pair? or Stream returns stream with Close(); we can add a convenience ContextClose in beta.

sam: Let's track this as a DX issue: small API change (add Close) + bugfix (select on ctx). Impact: any customers using streaming PRs may leak goroutines. Recommend patch release v0.9.2 with semver patch and a short migration note.

kai: Plan:
- PR today: add Stream.Close() and ensure Next() checks ctx.Done() (patch branch go/stream-cancel)
- run unit + integration repro harness
- cut v0.9.2 release and announce in release notes + devex channel

marta: Thanks! Assigning follow-up to @kai. If you want, add a small sample snippet to the quickstart showing proper Close() usage. Sample I propose:
```go
stream := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
defer stream.Close()
for {
  tok, err := stream.Next()
  if err != nil { handle(err); break }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```

kai: Yep will add sample, unit tests, and link to issue in PR. @josh can you help with the release notes blurb?

josh: Yep. Will draft notes and an internal alert to Eng SRE to watch for leaked goroutines in the next deploy.

marta: Cool. Thanks y'all. If anyone else hits this, please react with :eyes: and drop the gist.

sam: :thumbsup:

kai: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-redwood/pull/412 (wip). Will update here when CI passes.

devex-bot: CI status: pending — go-redwood#412

kai: CI fixed; tests pass. Merging in 10m.

devex-bot: merged commit 9f3b2a — go-redwood v0.9.2-rc1

marta: Verified locally with repro — stream.Next() returns context.Canceled and goroutine exits. Thanks!

josh: Nice. Follow-up: add a short note in changelog about Close() semantic and the recommended defer pattern.

marta: Added :white_check_mark: to the gist.

devex-bot: released go-redwood v0.9.2 with patch: go-sdk:stream.Close and ctx cancel propagation (changelog: https://changelogs.redwood.ai/go-redwood/0.9.2)

marta: closing the thread.
